result:
If I had the power to alter one fundamental aspect of the world, I would give every person an innate, unshakeable capacity for empathy—the kind that lets you viscerally feel another’s joys and pains as if they were your own.

Here’s why I’d choose that:

1. Conflict would lose much of its fuel. When you can truly inhabit someone else’s perspective, it becomes far harder to dehumanize, exploit, or harm them.
2. Cooperation would flourish. Shared understanding naturally drives collaboration on problems like poverty, climate change, and disease, because the boundaries of “us” and “them” blur.
3. Progress would accelerate. Empathy doesn’t erase disagreement, but it keeps debate constructive and solutions inclusive, making innovation more sustainable.
4. Personal fulfillment would deepen. Relationships, art, and even ordinary daily interactions all gain richness when people can resonate more fully with one another.

Technically we already possess the neural wiring for empathy, but it’s unevenly developed and easily overridden by fear, bias, or indifference. If that mental circuit were universally strong—reliably tugging us toward compassion in every decision, policy, or invention—it would shift countless other levers at once. The world would still be complex and imperfect, yet its default setting would tilt toward understanding rather than division, and most of the changes we hope to see—justice, sustainability, health, peace—would become far more attainable.
